title: Exhibitions Mark Third and Final Year of For Freedoms Residency at Corcoran School
summary: For Freedoms , an artist-led organization deepening civic engagement by centering artists as essential to shaping a free and pluralist society, presents two new exhibitions marking the third and final year of its three-year artist residency with the Corcoran School of the Arts and Design at the George Washington University. Night and Day, by artist Eric Gottesman, and Reflect, by artist Cannupa Hanska Luger, will be on view at the Corcoran October 28, 2026 – February 19, 2027. Night and Day centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma's controversial 1983 Amharic novel Oromay, written under Ethiopia’s Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. title: ATADA: What the bylaws actually say
summary: The change from Antique Tribal Art Dealers Association to Authentic Tribal Art Dealers Association substituted a consequential word. “Antique” primarily concerns age. “Authentic” raises questions of identity, authorship, cultural context and representation. For dealers, collectors, museums, appraisers and Indigenous artists, those distinctions have practical consequences. ATADA's current bylaws place authenticity at the center of the organization's definition of the material represented by its dealer members. title: Shannon's Fine Art Auctioneers announces over 200 lots for annual Fall Sale
summary: Shannon’s Fine Art Auctioneers will host their annual Fall Fine Art Auction on Thursday, October 29th at 6pm Eastern Time. The auction, featuring over 200 lots, will showcase examples of quality American art, Modern art, and European paintings. A rare painting attributed to Alfred Jacob Miller titled Green River leads the auction. Painted in 1851, this work depicts a rendezvous of Native Americans, fur traders, and pioneers. Miller first travelled to the Rocky Mountains in 1837 and made field sketches he used for later studio compositions. There are at least three other versions of this composition in museum collections. The painting is estimated to bring $200,000-$300,000.

title: Artemis Fine Arts brings ancient Near Eastern treasures and Japanese masterpieces to October 23 auction
summary: From a Sumerian limestone pendant carved nearly 5,000 years ago to the elaborate enamelwork and ivory sculpture of Meiji-period Japan, Artemis Fine Arts will bring together centuries of artistic traditions in an auction scheduled for Friday, October 23, 2026. The sale, titled Ancient Jewelry, Antiquities & Ethnographic Art , features approximately 246 lots spanning the ancient Mediterranean, the Near East, Asia, and other cultural traditions. Beginning at 11 a.m. Eastern Time, the auction offers collectors an opportunity to explore objects whose appeal extends beyond their decorative qualities to the histories, craftsmanship, and beliefs they represent. title: Basquiat's Leonardo inspired masterpiece headlining Christie's 21st Century Evening Sale
summary: Christie's announced a masterpiece by Jean-Michel Basquiat, Untitled (Leonardo and His Five Grotesque Heads), which will be offered in the 21st Century Evening Sale on November 19 during 20/21 Fall Marquee Week. The monumental 84 x 84-inch painting is Basquiat's interpretation of Leonardo DaVinci's celebrated Grotesque sketch from circa 1493, A man tricked by Gypsies (Formerly Five Grotesque Heads). It has been in the same private collection for over two decades, unseen by the public. Estimated in the region of $30 million, Untitled (Leonardo and His Five Grotesque Heads) will be the top lot of the sale. Ana Maria Celis, Head of Post-War and Contemporary Art, remarks: “We are delighted to present Untitled (Leonardo and His Five Grotesque Heads), a powerful masterwork by Jean Michel-Basquiat, as the leading highlight of November's 21st Century Evening Sale. title: Master of charcoal Lee Bae expands meditative practice in two-floor Paris survey
summary: The cycle of life beats at the heart of Lee Bae’s art. Widely recognized for his mastery of charcoal, the philosophical artist uses it to explore universal themes of destruction and renewal. Charcoal, made from wood burned by fire, symbolizes both nature’s destructive force and its potential for regeneration and reignition. For Lee Bae, charcoal embodies the life cycle, purification, the passage of time, and energy. It is nature transformed by fire. Born in South Korea in 1956, Lee Bae came of age amid his country’s collective trauma from the Japanese occupation during the Second World War, the hardships of the post-Korean War era, and the economic struggles of the 1960s and ‘70s. He attended Seoul’s Hongik University, where he studied art under Park Seo-Bo, considered the godfather of Dansaekhwa—a monochrome movement that rejected both Western and Japanese art traditions in favor of introspective, labor-intensive, highly repetitive

title: Sotheby's to offer $42 million group of late Picasso masterpieces from European family
summary: Sotheby's will present Picasso's Heroic Years: Masterpieces from a Prestigious European Family, a group of four works from the final chapter of one of the most inventive careers in the history of art, in the Modern Evening Auction during The New York Sales this November. The group is led by the monumental Femme nue et homme au fanion (1969, estimate $15–20 million), alongside Couple (1970), Le Peintre et son modèle (1964) and Nu (1972), together carrying a combined estimate of $30–42 million. Notably, the two principal paintings, Femme nue et homme au fanion and Couple, have remained out of public view since their exhibition in Pablo Picasso, 1969-1970 at the Palais des Papes in Avignon in 1970. Organized by Christian and Yvonne Zervos, the celebrated exhibition assembled more than one hundred recent works and served as a landmark affirmation of Picasso's late achievement. title: George Washington's personal gift to John Jay leads $12M Sotheby's Americana sale
summary: This December, Sotheby's will present the second installment of Reason and Revolution: Extraordinary Works from a Distinguished Private Collection, a dedicated single-owner auction devoted to the founding of the United States. Following the auction this month featuring landmark works of science on 20 October, part 2 in December is led by the copy of the first official printing of the Acts of Congress that George Washington presented to John Jay in December 1789, estimated at $8–12 million. Washington and Jay were, respectively, the first President of the United States and the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, and the volume is the only one of five similarly bound copies to remain in private hands. On 9 December 1789, George Washington, the nation's first President, presented this volume to John Jay, the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.

title: Alberta Pane Gallery presents Kreëmart retrospective across two Paris spaces
summary: Alberta Pane Gallery is presenting across its two Parisian spaces the exhibition Kreëmart: The Provocateurs of Experimental Consumption, a new exhibition in Paris devoted to the most significant collaborations between the Kreëmart production studio and numerous internationally renowned artists. The exhibition is accompanied by a critical text by Eugenio Viola. Founded in 2009 by Raphael Castoriano, the sensory art studio Kreëmart was born from a desire to bring contemporary artists and pastry chefs together around multisensory and performative creations, introducing a playful and participatory dimension to the traditional experience of contemplating art. Through works in which taste becomes an artistic medium in its own right, Kreëmart encourages audiences to move beyond the role of passive spectator and become active participants in the experience. title: Vintage rarities to independent creations highlights of Christie's Geneva Rare Watches Auction
summary: The Rare Watches auction on 9 November at the Four Seasons Hotel des Bergues, Geneva, will present an exceptional selection of vintage timepieces and contemporary independent creations, reflecting some of the touchpoints driving today's global watch collector. Historically significant vintage watches and the most sought-after works of contemporary independent watchmakers continue to be sought after by the international horological collector community, with timepieces offered in the Rare Watches sale exemplifying this. Independent makers have reshaped collecting tastes through their extraordinary creativity, technical innovation, rarity, and uncompromising craftsmanship, capturing the attention of seasoned connoisseurs and a new generation of enthusiasts alike. title: Whitney Museum presents 'Charles Burchfield: Elemental' exploring nature as a living force
summary: The Whitney Museum of American Art presents Charles Burchfield: Elemental, an exhibition exploring Charles Burchfield’s (1893–1967) lifelong pursuit of what he described as the “tremendous force of nature.” Drawn entirely from the Whitney’s collection, the presentation brings together ten watercolors created between 1916 and 1960, tracing more than four decades of the artist’s singular engagement with the natural world and his transformation of landscape into an expression of emotion, atmosphere, and spiritual intensity. Opening October 22, 2026, Charles Burchfield: Elemental spans Burchfield’s career, from the radical experimentation of his early works to the expansive, visionary landscapes of his later years. title: Joan Mitchell Foundation releases landmark report on artist legacy stewardship
summary: What happens to an artist’s work, archives, and ideas when they are gone? Who makes the decisions that drive who and what gets to be remembered? What stories and perspectives are at risk of being lost in times of accelerated cultural erasure? These questions are at the heart of a new report from the Joan Mitchell Foundation: Creating Future Memory: Building the Field of Artist Legacy Stewardship , available as a free PDF download via the Foundation’s website. Alongside this publication, the Foundation is also launching an online Legacy Field Map —a crowd-sourced directory designed to support connection, knowledge-sharing, and community among those working to preserve and celebrate artists' lives and work across the country. “With the release of the Creating Future

title: National Museum of Asian Art announces Allison Chance as its new Chief Advancement Officer
summary: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of Asian Art today announced Allison Fleming Chance as its next chief advancement officer (CAO). Chance joins the museum from the U.S. Soccer Federation, where she was the vice president of individual giving. She brings more than two decades fundraising and leadership experience at major arts and cultural institutions, including the Smithsonian. Chance previously served as a major gifts officer from 2012 to 2015 at the Institution’s central advancement office during its $1.5 billion comprehensive campaign. At the National Museum of Asian Art, Chance will help advance the museum’s Second Century Campaign, which focuses on building support to expand the museum’s impact as a global leader in understanding the arts, cultures and societies of Asia and their intersections with the United States. title: Collection Council selects work by Adebunmi Gbadebo for 2025-2026 acquisition
summary: The Block Museum of Art at Northwestern University announces the acquisition of Many Mornings Later (2025–26) by American artist Adebunmi Gbadebo, whose work is currently featured in the 2026 Venice Biennale. The large-scale handmade paper work was selected by The Block’s 2025–26 Collection Council, a group of donors whose contributions support the growth and care of the museum’s collection. Throughout the academic year, Council members participate in a collaborative process of learning, research, and discussion with artists and curators. Working within the year’s theme of abstraction, the Council considered a shortlist of artists nominated by members and The Block’s curatorial team before reaching consensus on Many Mornings Later and recommending it to the museum’s Acquisitions Committee. “The Collection

title: Yossi Milo Gallery presents Ibrahim Said's second solo exhibition, 'Shaping Time'
summary: Yossi Milo is presenting Shaping Time, Ibrahim Said’s second solo presentation with the gallery. The exhibition will open on Thursday, October 22 will be on view through Saturday, January 9, 2027. Shaping Time coincides with the conclusion of Said’s participation as one of three inaugural artists in The Metropolitan Museum of Art and Vacheron Constantin Artisan Residency. Centered on the preservation and reinterpretation of traditional craft, this 18-month residency granted Said sustained access to The Met’s collection. This period of research and close engagement with the museum’s holdings informed much of the development of this new body of work. Across sculpture, ceramic forms, and intricately constructed surfaces, Ibrahim Said considers time not as a fixed progression from past to future, but as a layered condition in which histories and imagined

title: Rediscovering the Maestro Daddesco and the art of manuscript illumination in Giotto's Florence
summary: Long before the printed book transformed the way knowledge circulated, the making of a manuscript was a remarkable collective undertaking. Scribes carefully copied texts by hand, artists filled pages with painted figures and elaborate decoration, and patrons commissioned books that expressed their devotion, wealth, learning, and social standing. In early fourteenth-century Florence, this world flourished alongside one of the most important transformations in the history of Western painting. As Giotto introduced a new sense of physical presence and emotional expression into monumental art, manuscript illuminators were developing their own responses to the changing artistic language of the city. title: Municipal Gallery of Athens presents Victoria Skarlatou: Between Heaven and Earth
summary: Between Heaven and Earth, the first solo exhibition and retrospective of Victoria Skarlatou’s work, will be held at the City of Athens Art Gallery from October 22 to November 22, 2026. After more than sixty years of continuous artistic creation, Skarlatou’s work will be presented publicly for the first time as a unified artistic universe. Bringing together sixty-one works from the 1960s to the present day, the exhibition traces the evolution of a highly distinctive visual language that moves between everyday experience, personal memory, social observation, and metaphysical inquiry. The artist describes herself as a “draughtswoman.” She trained and worked at the Doxiadis Office in the late 1960s, and this background remains central to the way she constructs her images. title: Anna Zorina Gallery presents Alexander Kaletski's 50-year cardboard survey
summary: Anna Zorina Gallery presents Cardboard Chapel, a solo exhibition by Alexander Kaletski that includes a fifty year retrospective of his painting on cardboard. The title draws from the Sistine Chapel as a monumental example of how patronage of the arts has been used to shape and disseminate ideas, beliefs and stories throughout history. Kaletski considers how this powerful force operates today and he finds it in the marketing that surrounds us. Nowadays, financial support funds the creation of logos, packaging, and taglines that carefully construct narratives designed to make products recognizable, desirable, and memorable. Kaletski takes these commercial images and removes them from their original purpose. Working directly on discarded cardboard packaging, he transforms logos, forms, and fragments of design into paintings

title: Karen Gunderson debuts blue pigments and black light-shift works at Yancey Richardson
summary: Yancey Richardson presents Dark Waves Rising, an exhibition of new paintings by Karen Gunderson, the artist’s first solo exhibition in New York in over ten years and first with the gallery since joining in 2025. Gunderson will debut paintings from two bodies of work, Moon and Water, that have been unfolding and evolving over several decades. Dark Waves Rising sees Gunderson continuing her pursuit of the haptic with paintings that shift and adapt to their environment through an intensely rich surface texture that brings each scene beyond a purely visual register of experience. On November 7th Yancey Richardson will host Gunderson in conversation with Margaret Andera, Senior Curator of Contemporary Art at the Milwaukee Art Museum. The exhibition will be on view from October 22 through December 19, 2026. Over

title: National Museum of American History acquires costumes from the Broadway musical "Hadestown"
summary: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History received a donation of costumes today from the Tony and Grammy Award-winning Broadway musical Hadestown in a ceremony following its matinee performance in New York City. Hadestown follows two intertwining love stories from Greek mythology—the young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice and the inharmonious King Hades and his wife Persephone—and invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. The museum will receive the green dress, boots, choker and flower headpiece of Ani DiFranco’s Persephone costume, and the jacket, trousers, vest, shirt, tie and snakeskin boots of Patrick Page’s Hades. “Hadestown is a deeply resonant piece of theater that connects ancient myth with modern struggles, reminding us of the enduring power of love

title: Palais de Tokyo presents Sonia Gomes's textile-based survey of memory and resistance
summary: Sonia Gomes approaches textiles as vectors of memory and history, transforming them into quasi-organic sculptures. Drawing on her Afro-Brazilian heritage, she weaves sensory narratives at once intimate and collective. This exhibition offers a sensory journey through the universe of Sonia Gomes, where the intimate, the collective and the sacred are woven together. Through found or gifted textiles as well as rope, embroidery, fragments of wood or other recycled objects, she composes sculptures, paintings and installations which unfold into space stories of transmission and transformation. Knotted, plaited, assembled or embroidered, the materials bear the traces of their past lives and become vectors of sensory memory. Suspended, hung on the wall or placed on the floor, these works resemble living organisms whose forms seem to unfold

title: Malmö Konsthall hosts Otobong Nkanga's first major Scandinavian retrospective
summary: Since the late 1990s, Otobong Nkanga has explored themes related to ecology and the relationships between the body and territory. Through her multidisciplinary practice, she has been delving deeply into issues such as mining extraction and the use of the earth’s resources, but also the body and its connection to space and the earth. The notion of strata is central both in the materiality of Nkanga’s works and in her way of thinking about the relationships between human beings and the places they inhabit and transform—and in which they are also transformed themselves. She simultaneously observes the circulation of materials, goods and people, their intermingled histories and their exploitation, marked by the residue of environmental violence. While questioning memory, she offers a vision of a possible future. Otobong Nkanga was born in 1974 in Kano

title: 'Chez Sotheby's': Auction house merges dining and fine art during Art Basel Paris
summary: Now open through 24 October, during Art Basel Paris, Sotheby’s and _POLIMENO present Chez Sotheby’s, a living environment bringing together art, dining and cultural exchange within an extraordinary Parisian apartment. Neither an exhibition nor a restaurant in the conventional sense, Chez Sotheby’s brings exceptional works of Modern, Post-War and Contemporary Art into a setting designed for gathering, discovery and dialogue. Located at 242 Rue de Rivoli, overlooking the Jardin des Tuileries and steps from both Art Basel Paris and Sotheby's Paris, Chez Sotheby's reimagines a long European tradition in which collecting is as much about gathering as it is about acquiring. For one week only, it will become part of the rhythm of Paris: a destination between openings and appointments where connections are forged and discoveries happen naturally.

title: Armenian Museum of America presents Beyond the Curtain: Materiality and Devotion in Armenian Art
summary: The Armenian Museum of America announced the opening of Beyond the Curtain: Materiality and Devotion in Armenian Art on October 22. This new exhibition includes more than 20 objects from the Museum’s collection, and it is curated by Anahit Gasparyan. The exhibition examines Armenian religious art through the materials that have shaped devotional experiences, inviting visitors to consider how faith becomes tangible through art, ritual, craftsmanship, and sacred objects. At the heart of the exhibition is the Mardin Altar Curtain, a remarkable textile that provides a point of entry into the material and visual world of Armenian religious practice. This piece was exhibited at the Tufts University Art Galleries in 2021. The exhibition is also anchored by the Garabed Gospel, which was completed in the year 1207, connecting the presentation

title: Latvian National Museum of Art presents environmental exhibition 'A Journey to Marsi'
summary: From 22 October to 15 November 2026, the 3rd floor vestibule of the main building of the Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga (Jaņa Rozentāla laukums 1) hosts A Journey to Marsi. An Artist Enters a Wooded Meadow, an exhibition created jointly by the Latvian Fund for Nature and artists Kristaps Kalns and Sarmīte Māliņa. This collaborative project is dedicated to wooded meadows, one of Latvia’s rarest and most biodiverse landscapes. Through large-scale photographs, the exhibition presents eight encounters between Latvian artists or artist groups and this distinctive landscape across the seasons, alongside the artists’ impressions and memories of their journeys.
